walkthroughs.body_html:
Religion & Ethics: Ethical Theory & Application — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Religion & Ethics: Ethical Theory & Application brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Religion & Ethics: Ethical Theory & Application.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does utilitarianism say is right action?
options: Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.
Whatever makes you personally happy is the right thing to do.
Virtue ethics is about following the Ten Commandments.
The action that produces the greatest happiness for the greatest number — judged by consequences, not intentions or rules.

mcqs.q: What does Kant's categorical imperative require?
options: Do whatever your conscience tells you to do.
Treat others how you would like to be treated.
Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.
Acting only on maxims you could will to be universal laws, and treating people as ends in themselves, never merely as means.

mcqs.q: What is the focus of virtue ethics?
options: Virtue ethics tells you which specific actions are right and wrong.
Virtue ethics is about following the Ten Commandments.
Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.
On character and habits — becoming the kind of person who acts well, aiming at eudaimonia (flourishing) through practising virtues that lie between extremes.

mcqs.q: A rule utilitarian refuses to torture a suspect even when it might maximise utility in this one case, because:
options: a general rule against torture produces more happiness overall than allowing case-by-case exceptions
torture violates the categorical imperative
pain can never be measured
the suspect's natural rights are God-given

mcqs.q: Mill's distinction between higher and lower pleasures is a response to the objection that utilitarianism is:
options: 'a doctrine worthy of swine', valuing only bodily pleasure
too demanding for ordinary people
unable to predict consequences
indifferent to the greatest number

mcqs.q: Applying natural law to euthanasia, a follower of Aquinas would most likely argue that:
options: intentionally killing an innocent patient violates the precept of preserving life, though proportionate pain relief may be permitted under double effect
the most loving outcome should always decide the case
euthanasia is right if the majority of citizens approve it
quality of life outweighs sanctity of life

mcqs.q: Fletcher would judge an action right if and only if it:
options: produces the most loving outcome in that particular situation
follows the church's moral rules without exception
maximises the agent's own happiness
is approved by conscience understood as God's voice
